title: Strict naturality of evaluation from comma-chain simplicial replacement
statement:
Use simplicial sets, nerves and simplicial replacements $\mathrm{BK}$ as in [lem-coef-bousfield-kan-comparison-calculus] and [def-coef-zigzag-homotopy-calculus]. Let $P:A\to C$ be a functor between small categories and $X:C\to\mathrm{sSet}$ a diagram. For $c\in C$ the category $C/c$ has objects $t:d\to c$ and arrows $h:(d,t)\to(d',t')$ with $t'h=t$. Form the bisimplicial set
$$V(P,X)_{i,q}=\coprod_{x_0\to\cdots\to x_i\text{ in }A}\ \coprod_{(c_0,t_0)\to\cdots\to(c_q,t_q)\text{ in }C/Px_0}X(c_0)_q.$$
In the $q$ direction use the $\mathrm{BK}$ operators on the displayed slice chain and $X$ factor. In the $i$ direction $d_0$ postcomposes every $t_a$ by $P(v_1)$ for $v_1:x_0\to x_1$; other faces compose or delete arrows of the $A$ chain and degeneracies insert identities. Let $U(P,X)_{i,q}=\coprod_{x_0\to\cdots\to x_i}X(Px_0)_q$, with first $i$ face applying $X(Pv_1)$, the other $i$ operators on the chain, and $q$ operators on $X$. Then $\operatorname{diag}U(P,X)=\mathrm{BK}_A(XP)$, and
$$e_{P,X}:V(P,X)\to U(P,X),\quad (x_\bullet,(c_\bullet,t_\bullet),z)\mapsto(x_\bullet,X(t_0)z)$$
is a bisimplicial map.

For functors $K:A'\to A$, $H:C'\to C$, $P':A'\to C'$ with $PK=HP'$, a diagram $X':C'\to\mathrm{sSet}$ and a natural transformation $\eta:X'\Rightarrow XH$, define $V':V(P',X')\to V(P,X)$ by $K$ on the $A'$ chain, $H$ on the slice chain and $\eta_{c'_0}$ on $z$; define $U':U(P',X')\to U(P,X)$ by $K$ on the $A'$ chain and $\eta_{P'x'_0}$ on its coefficient. These are bisimplicial maps and $U'e_{P',X'}=e_{P,X}V'$ strictly. All these induced maps preserve identities and composition in $(K,H,\eta)$ strictly. Consequently their diagonal maps form the same strictly commutative square. No equivalence condition on any of these data is required.

source.place: Dwyer–Kan, Calculating simplicial localizations, proof 9.10, printed pp.32–33: regrouping by A-chains, evaluation of terminal-slice augmentation, and its strict naturality. No Stacks tag states this categorical bar calculation; source formulas checked online, agent expansion of strict naturality.

proof.text: For an $A$-chain write $v_{ab}:x_a\to x_b$ for its composite, with $v_{aa}=1$. For $\alpha:[j]\to[i]$ define the $i$ operator of $V$ by restricting the chain to $x_{\alpha(0)}\to\cdots\to x_{\alpha(j)}$ and replacing every $t_a$ by $P(v_{0,\alpha(0)})t_a$, leaving $c_\bullet,z$ fixed. This remains a slice chain because $(P(v_{0,\alpha(0)})t_{a+1})h_{a+1}=P(v_{0,\alpha(0)})t_a$. For $U$ use the same restricted $A$-chain and replace $y$ by $X(P(v_{0,\alpha(0)}))y$. These give exactly the stated faces and degeneracies. Identities have $v_{00}=1$; for $\gamma:[k]\to[j]$, the two coefficient/postcomposition arrows multiply to $P(v_{\alpha(0),\alpha\gamma(0)})P(v_{0,\alpha(0)})=P(v_{0,\alpha\gamma(0)})$. Thus both families satisfy the contravariant functor laws in the $i$ variable, as required by the definition of simplicial set in [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set].

source.place: Dwyer–Kan, Calculating simplicial localizations, proof 9.10, printed pp.32–33 (PDF pp.16–17); agent expansion of the chain formulas, with no homotopy-equivalence claim used.

proof.text: For a fixed $A$-chain, the $q$ row of $V$ is $\mathrm{BK}_{C/Px_0}(X\circ\operatorname{dom})$, where $\operatorname{dom}(d,t)=d$ and $\operatorname{dom}(h)=h$; the row of $U$ is $X(Px_0)$. The displayed $\mathrm{BK}$ operators in [lem-coef-bousfield-kan-comparison-calculus] supply the $q$ simplicial laws. Explicitly, if $\beta:[r]\to[q]$ and $h_{ab}:c_a\to c_b$ denotes the composite in the slice chain, its $V$ operator restricts the chain to $(c_{\beta(b)},t_{\beta(b)})$ and sends $z$ to $X(h_{0,\beta(0)})\beta^*z$; here $\beta^*$ is the operator of $X(c_0)$ and the component of $X(h)$ is taken in degree $r$. This commutes with the $i$ operator of step 1: restriction selects the same $t_{\beta(b)}$, postcomposition applies the same $P(v_{0,\alpha(0)})$, and neither changes the other's $c,h,z$ operations. For $U$ the mixed identity is $\beta^*X(Pv)y=X(Pv)\beta^*y$, since $X(Pv)$ is a simplicial map. Hence $V$ and $U$ are bisimplicial sets.

source.place: Dwyer–Kan, Calculating simplicial localizations, proof 9.10, printed pp.32–33 (PDF pp.16–17); agent expansion of the chain formulas, with no homotopy-equivalence claim used.

proof.text:
Evaluation commutes with every $i$ operator of step 1 because $X(P(v_{0,\alpha(0)}))X(t_0)=X(P(v_{0,\alpha(0)})t_0)$. For the $q$ operator of step 2 the slice equation is $t_{\beta(0)}h_{0,\beta(0)}=t_0$, including $\beta(0)=0$. Consequently evaluation after that operator sends the coefficient to
$$X(t_{\beta(0)})X(h_{0,\beta(0)})\beta^*z=X(t_0)\beta^*z=\beta^*X(t_0)z,$$
which is the $q$ operator after evaluation. The last equality uses that $X(t_0)$ is a morphism of simplicial sets, that is a natural transformation as defined in [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set]. The $A$-chain agrees on both sides. Thus the stated $e_{P,X}$ is a bisimplicial map.

source.place: Dwyer–Kan, Calculating simplicial localizations, proof 9.10, printed pp.32–33 (PDF pp.16–17); agent expansion of the chain formulas, with no homotopy-equivalence claim used.

proof.text:
The formula for $V'$ is well typed: $H(t'_a):Hc'_a\to HP'x'_0=PKx'_0$ and $H(t'_{a+1})H(h'_{a+1})=H(t'_a)$. The coefficient has the required type since $\eta_{c'_0}:X'(c'_0)\to X(Hc'_0)$ is a simplicial map. The $U'$ coefficient has target $X(HP'x'_0)=X(PKx'_0)$. In the $i$ variable, $K$ preserves the selected composites and
$$H(P'(v')t')=P(Kv')H(t'),$$
using $HP'=PK$ on morphisms; this proves compatibility for $V'$. For $U'$ compatibility is exactly
$$\eta_{P'b'}X'(P'v')=X(HP'v')\eta_{P'a'}=X(PKv')\eta_{P'a'}$$
for the first selected arrow $v':a'\to b'$. In the $q$ variable, $H$ preserves all selected composites; compatibility on coefficients is
$$\eta_{c'_b}X'(h'_{0b})(\beta^*z)=X(Hh'_{0b})\beta^*(\eta_{c'_0}z),\qquad b=\beta(0).$$
This is naturality of $\eta$ for $h'_{0b}$ followed by simplicial naturality of its component. For $U'$ only the component's simplicial naturality is needed. Thus $V'$ and $U'$ commute with every operator; by [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set] they are maps in both simplicial variables.

source.place: Dwyer–Kan, Calculating simplicial localizations, proof 9.10, printed pp.32–33 (PDF pp.16–17); agent expansion of the chain formulas, with no homotopy-equivalence claim used.

proof.text: For a generator $(x'_\bullet,(c'_\bullet,t'_\bullet),z)$ the two composites in the proposed square have the identical $A$-chain $Kx'_\bullet$. Their coefficients are respectively $\eta_{P'x'_0}X'(t'_0)z$ and $X(Ht'_0)\eta_{c'_0}z$. They agree by the defining naturality square of the given $\eta$ at the arrow $t'_0:c'_0\to P'x'_0$. The equality holds in every bidegree on every summand, so $U'e_{P',X'}=e_{P,X}V'$ as functions, hence as bisimplicial maps. This is an equality, with no chosen homotopy or equivalence data.

source.place: Dwyer–Kan, Calculating simplicial localizations, proof 9.10, printed pp.32–33 (PDF pp.16–17); agent expansion of the chain formulas, with no homotopy-equivalence claim used.

proof.text: For an identity triple $(1_A,1_C,1_X)$, every chain, slice arrow and coefficient is unchanged, so both induced maps are identities. To check composition, take a further triple $(L:A''\to A',J:C''\to C',\theta:X''\Rightarrow X'J)$ with $P'L=JP''$. Its composite with $(K,H,\eta)$ is $(KL,HJ,\lambda)$, where $\lambda_d=\eta_{Jd}\circ\theta_d:X''(d)\to X(HJd)$; the required equality is $PKL=HP'L=HJP''$. Applying the two $V$ maps gives the chains $KLx''_\bullet$, $HJ(c''_\bullet,t''_\bullet)$ and coefficient $\eta_{Jc''_0}\theta_{c''_0}z=\lambda_{c''_0}z$, exactly the direct formula. The two $U$ maps give coefficient $\eta_{JP''x''_0}\theta_{P''x''_0}y=\lambda_{P''x''_0}y$, again the direct formula. Function composition and functor composition are associative and unital, so these identities are strict. All that was used is the given functor and natural-transformation data.

source.place: Dwyer–Kan, Calculating simplicial localizations, proof 9.10, printed pp.32–33 (PDF pp.16–17); agent expansion of the chain formulas, with no homotopy-equivalence claim used.

proof.text: In bidegree $(n,n)$, $U$ is $\coprod_{x_0\to\cdots\to x_n}X(Px_0)_n$. Applying the same $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$ in both directions gives the restricted $A$-chain and coefficient $X(P(v_{0,\alpha(0)}))\alpha^*y$. These are precisely the $\mathrm{BK}_A(XP)$ operators of [lem-coef-bousfield-kan-comparison-calculus], including the first face and identity insertion. Thus $\operatorname{diag}U=\mathrm{BK}_A(XP)$ with its displayed model. By the diagonal definition in that node, restriction of each bisimplicial map to bidegrees $(n,n)$ is a simplicial map. Restricting the pointwise equality of step 5 and the identity/composition equalities of step 6 gives the asserted strictly commutative diagonal square and strict functoriality. None of these calculations requires any equivalence assumption.

lean.statement: theorem evaluation_naturality : (∀ D : Data.{u}, BousfieldKan.diagonal (Functor.curry.obj (U D)) = BousfieldKan.BK D.A (D.P ⋙ D.X)) ∧ (∀ {D E : Data.{u}} (f : Change D E), evaluation D ≫ UChange f = VChange f ≫ evaluation E) ∧ (∀ D : Data.{u}, VChange (identity D) = 𝟙 _ ∧ UChange (identity D) = 𝟙 _) ∧ (∀ {D E F : Data.{u}} (f : Change D E) (g : Change E F), VChange (compose f g) = VChange f ≫ VChange g ∧ UChange (compose f g) = UChange f ≫ UChange g) ∧ (∀ {D E : Data.{u}} (f : Change D E), Functor.whiskerLeft (Functor.diag SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ) (evaluation D) ≫ Functor.whiskerLeft (Functor.diag SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ) (UChange f) = Functor.whiskerLeft (Functor.diag SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ) (VChange f) ≫ Functor.whiskerLeft (Functor.diag SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ) (evaluation E))
lean.note: Explicit slice-chain dependent sums reuse BKObj and BKMap. Product-index functors are the two bisimplicial sets.
